title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: For every planar graph $H$, the Erdős-Pósa property holds for $H$-models with a $O(k \log k)$ bounding function.
context_text: An $H$-model in $G$ is a collection $\{S_x: x\in V(H)\}$ of vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of $G$ such that $S_x$ and $S_y$ are joined by an edge of $G$ whenever $xy\in E(H)$ (so $G$ has an $H$-model iff $H$ is a minor of $G$). Let $\nu_H(G)$ be the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint $H$-models in $G$ and $\tau_H(G)$ the minimum size of a set $X$ with $G-X$ having no $H$-model. The Erdős–Pósa property holds for $H$-models with bounding function $f$ if $\tau_H(G)\le f(\nu_H(G))$ for every graph $G$; Robertson and Seymour proved it holds for some $f$ if and only if $H$ is planar. Chekuri and Chuzhoy showed there are integers $a,b,c$ such that for every planar $H$ on $h$ vertices one can take $f(k)=ah^b\,k\log^c(k+1)$ ($c$ apparently a double-digit integer), derived from their result that there are $a',b',c'$ such that every graph of treewidth at least $a'r^{b'}k\log^{c'}(k+1)$ has $k$ vertex-disjoint subgraphs of treewidth at least $r$; this approach loses a $\log k$ factor ($c=c'+1$), and $c'\ge1$ is necessary, so it always gives $c\ge2$. For planar $H$ containing a cycle there is an $\Omega(k\log k)$ lower bound (from Erdős and Pósa's triangle case, or from graphs of linear treewidth and logarithmic girth), and for forests $H$ the right order is $O(k)$, so the conjecture would settle the growth rate for all planar $H$. It was known for cycles (Fiorini and Herinckx; Erdős–Pósa for triangles) and for multigraphs consisting of two vertices joined by parallel edges. The paper proves it for all wheels $W_t$ ($t\ge3$, a cycle of length $t$ plus a vertex adjacent to all its vertices), which also covers all minors of wheels, since an $O(k\log k)$ bounding function is preserved under taking minors of $H$.
paper_title: A tight Erdős-Pósa function for wheel minors

title: Conjecture 1.4
